planting.note: Direct sow after all danger of frost has passed and soil has warmed, or start indoors 4-6 weeks early for an earlier bloom flush.

directions: Benary's Giant Wine produces fully double, dahlia-like blooms in a deep burgundy-wine shade on sturdy stems that hold up well in the field and in the vase. Sow seed directly in full sun after the soil has warmed, or start indoors for a head start, then thin seedlings to about a foot apart to promote airflow and reduce powdery mildew. Plants branch readily and rebloom continuously through summer when spent flowers are cut or deadheaded regularly. The rich, saturated color pairs especially well with lime-green and cream-toned zinnias in mixed cutting-garden bouquets.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost once soil is warm, or start indoors a few weeks early for an earlier first flush.

directions: Benary's Giant Lime carries unusual chartreuse-green, fully double flowers up to 5 inches across atop tall, upright stems bred for commercial cut-flower production. Direct sow after the last frost in warm, fertile soil, spacing plants roughly a foot apart to keep foliage dry and minimize disease. The unique lime-green color holds well after cutting and is prized by florists for filling out mixed-color bouquets with an unexpected accent. Deadhead or harvest stems regularly to keep new buds forming from midsummer until the first fall frost.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost once soil is warm, or transplant indoor-started seedlings after hardening off.

directions: Benary's Giant Salmon Rose bears large, fully double flowers in a soft coral-pink shade on strong three-to-four-foot stems well suited to cutting-garden rows. Sow directly in full sun once the soil is reliably warm, or transplant indoor-started seedlings after hardening off, spacing plants about a foot apart. Regular harvesting or deadheading keeps the branching plants producing new blooms from early summer right up to frost. Water at the base rather than overhead to keep foliage dry and reduce the risk of powdery mildew in humid weather.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers

planting.note: Direct sow after frost danger has passed in warm soil, or get a jump on the season with an indoor start.

directions: Benary's Giant Coral produces vivid coral-orange, fully double blooms up to 5-6 inches wide on vigorous, tall plants bred specifically for professional cut-flower growers. Direct sow after frost danger has passed in warm soil, or get a jump on the season with an indoor start, then space seedlings a foot apart for good airflow. The warm coral tone stands out mixed with the series' other colors in market bouquets and holds its brightness well through a long vase life. Keep plants picked or deadheaded to encourage continuous branching and flower production through the growing season.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers

common_name: ProCut Gold Sunflower (Single-Stem Golden-Yellow Cut Flower)

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost once soil has warmed above 60F, and stagger plantings every 1-2 weeks for a steady cut-flower harvest through the season.

directions: ProCut Gold is a single-stem, pollen-free sunflower in the industry-standard ProCut line, producing one uniform golden-yellow bloom per plant on a tall, unbranched stem ideal for bunching. Sow seed a half-inch deep on tight spacing so plants put their energy into one strong stem rather than side branches, and expect the whole planting to flower together in a tight window around 55-65 days. Because the flowers carry no pollen, they stay clean in mixed arrangements and last longer without shedding on tablecloths or fabric. Succession sow every week or two through midsummer to keep a steady supply of stems for cutting.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers

common_name: ProCut Plum Sunflower (Single-Stem Reddish-Purple Cut Flower)

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost once soil has warmed above 60F, and stagger plantings every 1-2 weeks for a steady cut-flower harvest through the season.

directions: ProCut Plum is the deep reddish-purple member of the ProCut single-stem sunflower series, valued by cut-flower growers for its unusual wine-toned petals surrounding a dark center. Direct sow a half-inch deep in full sun after the last frost, spacing plants closely so each one channels its growth into a single unbranched stem topped by one bloom. The entire planting matures and flowers together roughly 55-65 days after sowing, simplifying harvest for market bunches. Being pollen-free, the blooms hold up cleanly in mixed bouquets, and cutting at the first sign of petals unfurling gives the longest vase life.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers

common_name: SunRich Gold Sunflower (Pollen-Free Single-Stem Golden Cut Flower)

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost once soil has warmed, and plant successive rounds every 1-2 weeks for a continuous cut-flower supply.

directions: SunRich Gold produces a single rich golden-yellow bloom per plant on an unbranched stem, part of the pollen-free SunRich series bred for the commercial cut-flower trade. Sow seed directly in full sun after the last frost on tight spacing so the plants grow tall and single-stemmed rather than branching. Because the flowers shed no pollen, they stay tidy in floral arrangements and won't stain tablecloths or clothing. Plant successive rounds every week or two through early summer for a continuous supply of uniform, same-day-blooming stems.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers
